tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# Submission and pitch

What to hand in for the Tacto track, and how the pitch works. Deadline: **Sunday 12:00 on ehl.gg**.

## What to submit

1. **Your repo:** the agent and a README that says how to run it (setup, the environment variables it
   needs, without values, and the command). Put the **commit hash** your agent runs in the final into
   the description. The jury and tum.ai must be able to open the repo; tum.ai runs a code agent over
   every submission.
2. **A short description** of your approach: how your agent prepares, what it reads in the data, how
   it decides what to offer, and when it closes or walks away.
3. **Slides** for the pitch. The top 10 present them from 13:00.

Keep every key out of the repo: no `.env`, no LLM key, no arena key.

## At 12:00 your agent is already running

The code freeze and the Live Final start together, so start your agent before 12:00 and leave it
running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

Or your own runner that polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`. The kit's runner waits for wave 1, plays each
wave's cases in parallel within the 8-minute cap and stops after the fifth wave. From 12:00 there is no
human in the loop, and your agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard` or `/results`.
We check the top 10 for pushes after the freeze.

Checklist for 11:30:

- The machine and network you use for the final; one practice case went through it at the 09:00
  pre-flight.
- `uv run arena data` ran after 08:00, so the Sunday release sits next to the package.
- `uv run arena me` answers with your team: the key works.
- LLM credits and rate limits for about an hour of parallel play.
- The runner is started and logs to a file; the laptop is on power and does not sleep.

## The pitch

- **The top 10:** the ten teams with the most points after the five waves.
- **5 minutes pitch + 2 minutes of questions**, from 13:00. tum.ai keeps the time; the slot does not
  stretch.
- **Every replay is open to the jury.** After the final, each case on https://arena.tacto.ai/results
  links to its replay. Pick one negotiation and walk us through it.
- Questions to expect: Why did your agent write that? Would it have worked on a real supplier? What
  did your agent learn about suppliers, and from where?
- ⟦Q2: how the Live Final score and the jury combine for places 1-3, and the jury criteria⟧

1	# Agent design
2	
3	What the buyer does today. Observations behind it are in `learnings.md`; the module map with
4	every file is `architecture.md`; the diagram is on page 1 of [writeup.pdf](../writeup/writeup.pdf).
5	
6	## Principle
7	
8	Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes words.
9	Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.
10	
11	## A case
12	
13	1. **Prepare**: open the session, read the quote and standard terms, build the supplier's
14	   profile and the claim bank, estimate its full cost and cost of money, plan the opening terms
15	   and price.
16	2. **Negotiate**, one thread per supplier, in parallel. Each round: read the reply (its sheets,
17	   asks, signals), plan candidate sheets with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`, decide counter,
18	   accept or walk, write the e-mail (model paragraph with a hard timeout, template if late),
19	   guard every field and claim, send.
20	3. **Close**: accept the best standing sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk;
21	   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.
22	
23	## Modules
24	
25	| Module | Job |
26	|---|---|
27	| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate; a quoted package kept exactly as quoted (`quoted_offer`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value`, overtime for faster delivery); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price; the index-clause trade (the supplier's clause value capped at 8 % of the price, none for a hedged supplier) |
28	| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
29	| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks, news and the supplier's own e-mails, cost of money |
30	| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and signals, a share of the gap per round, held after a deep first concession, a patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts a quoted package when it beats our plan at equal value to the supplier, mirrors a better alternative, takes or offers an index clause; bounds the full-cost estimate by what the supplier itself offers, valued to it, so the relationship target never sits above its counter; never proposes above the price where C meets the alternative, and answers a final word it would refuse with one sheet at that ceiling before the close; the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; deduplicates forecasts from the same period and suppresses unchanged offers; evaluates explicit supplier needs as complete, must-have-safe packages only when total cost improves; closes on final offer, agreement or round limit |
31	| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph answering the supplier's last e-mail and asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else a deterministic fallback), then code sentences with figures, claims and the proposal; forecast rows as CSV when proof is asked; tracks model attempts, successes, timeouts, rejections and deadline skips |
32	| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when the arena refuses a send; a non-repeating fallback for failed policy moves; the model's time budgeted so every live clock gets a message; Live Final waves never raise and resume a crashed case |
33	
34	When a relationship-goal counter reaches or falls below our estimated target, the policy stops
35	offering and the close gate evaluates the supplier's standing sheet.
36	
37	## Subagent team
38	
39	Before negotiation, `buyer/research.py` assigns four specialists to supplier data groups and has a
40	lead choose up to two allowed term trades, claim order and tone. `buyer/rehearsal.py` prepares
41	possible supplier arguments and evidence-based responses. During negotiation,
42	`buyer/analyst.py` classifies each reply for tone and a steady, hold or argue tactic; code still
43	controls price and terms.
44	After a case, `buyer/memory.py` writes a debrief to `buyer/lessons.jsonl` for later research. All
45	model output is bounded and validated; failures fall back to code-owned behavior.
46	
47	## Supplier estimate
48	
49	`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
50	`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost`. We estimate full cost from
51	`should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, capped at the quote less the sustainable margin
52	in relationship goals; cost of money from owner type, cash signals and cash discounts; overtime
53	from capacity signals. The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are
54	read at runtime through the ID index.
55	
56	[agentic-approach.md](agentic-approach.md) is a proposal for a model-chosen tactic inside these
57	boundaries; not implemented.

# Agent design

What the buyer does today. Observations behind it are in `learnings.md`; the module map with
every file is `architecture.md`; the diagram is on page 1 of [writeup.pdf](../writeup/writeup.pdf).

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes words.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare**: open the session, read the quote and standard terms, build the supplier's
   profile and the claim bank, estimate its full cost and cost of money, plan the opening terms
   and price.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread per supplier, in parallel. Each round: read the reply (its sheets,
   asks, signals), plan candidate sheets with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`, decide counter,
   accept or walk, write the e-mail (model paragraph with a hard timeout, template if late),
   guard every field and claim, send.
3. **Close**: accept the best standing sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.

## Modules

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate; a quoted package kept exactly as quoted (`quoted_offer`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value`, overtime for faster delivery); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price; the index-clause trade (the supplier's clause value capped at 8 % of the price, none for a hedged supplier) |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks, news and the supplier's own e-mails, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and signals, a share of the gap per round, held after a deep first concession, a patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts a quoted package when it beats our plan at equal value to the supplier, mirrors a better alternative, takes or offers an index clause; bounds the full-cost estimate by what the supplier itself offers, valued to it, so the relationship target never sits above its counter; never proposes above the price where C meets the alternative, and answers a final word it would refuse with one sheet at that ceiling before the close; the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; deduplicates forecasts from the same period and suppresses unchanged offers; evaluates explicit supplier needs as complete, must-have-safe packages only when total cost improves; closes on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph answering the supplier's last e-mail and asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else a deterministic fallback), then code sentences with figures, claims and the proposal; forecast rows as CSV when proof is asked; tracks model attempts, successes, timeouts, rejections and deadline skips |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when the arena refuses a send; a non-repeating fallback for failed policy moves; the model's time budgeted so every live clock gets a message; Live Final waves never raise and resume a crashed case |

When a relationship-goal counter reaches or falls below our estimated target, the policy stops
offering and the close gate evaluates the supplier's standing sheet.

## Subagent team

Before negotiation, `buyer/research.py` assigns four specialists to supplier data groups and has a
lead choose up to two allowed term trades, claim order and tone. `buyer/rehearsal.py` prepares
possible supplier arguments and evidence-based responses. During negotiation,
`buyer/analyst.py` classifies each reply for tone and a steady, hold or argue tactic; code still
controls price and terms.
After a case, `buyer/memory.py` writes a debrief to `buyer/lessons.jsonl` for later research. All
model output is bounded and validated; failures fall back to code-owned behavior.

## Supplier estimate

`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost`. We estimate full cost from
`should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, capped at the quote less the sustainable margin
in relationship goals; cost of money from owner type, cash signals and cash discounts; overtime
from capacity signals. The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are
read at runtime through the ID index.

[agentic-approach.md](agentic-approach.md) is a proposal for a model-chosen tactic inside these
boundaries; not implemented.

# Learnings

## Louis subagent-team practice batch (2026-10-11)

One hosted Practice session was run for each available case. All ten reached a deal; the mean
score was 0.7772. The dashboard reference at the time was 0.802, but this single batch is not a
paired comparison and does not establish a reliable gain or regression.

| Case | Score |
|---|---:|
| P01 | 0.9085 |
| P02 | 0.7347 |
| P03 | 0.9276 |
| P04 | 0.8604 |
| P05 | 0.8218 |
| P07 | 0.7313 |
| P08 | 0.7036 |
| P10 | 0.6785 |
| P11 | 0.7099 |
| P18 | 0.6957 |

The run recorded 127 subagent attempts, 121 successes and 6 timeouts; the writer had 37 attempts,
29 successes, 7 rejected paragraphs, 2 deadline skips and 1 timeout. Fallbacks kept sessions
running. These counts describe model reliability, not its effect on scores. The batch used the
`louis/subagent-team` base with the candidate safeguards; it is diagnostic evidence only.

Observations from the arena and the data package, with evidence. An entry says what happened and
how often, not what to do; what the agent does is in `design.md`. Most entries rest on one to
three sessions with one supplier. The sandbox bots are deterministic per sheet path; the practice
suppliers vary 1 to 2 % between runs with the same sheets. Sessions: `exports/` (schema in
`exports/README.md`), `logs/sessions/`, `logs/runs/`. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
the package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit.

## Where we stand (Saturday night)

Mean of best scores 0.776, rank 3 of 24 on the practice board (first 0.838); the last ten-case
validation run of one code version averaged 0.727. Record = best of all teams on `/v1/live`,
house agent in brackets; records average 0.84.

| Case | Goal | Ours | Deal | Record (house) |
....
- No alternative, so a walk-away scores 0: D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17. Contract length or volume
  is ours to pick in 14 of 21 cases. Only a standing sheet can be accepted (an alternative
  returns 422); a better alternative sent back as our sheet became standing (P10).
- The kit's `complete_offer` snaps values and can replace an explicit allowed `None` with the
  first option (`economics.quoted_offer` keeps a quoted package as quoted).

## Supplier behaviour (`arena`)

- **Round 1, D01 (sandbox foundry, 30 runs, quote 52.90):** anchors 44.0 to 48.5 without claims
  all got 51.30; should-cost claim alone 51.00, order prices alone 50.30, notice or scorecard
  alone 51.30, all three 50.00, the same three at anchor 48.88 50.40; anchor 37.03 got 52.30,
  50.60 got 51.40.
- **Round 1, distributors P08 and P18 (15 runs):** anchors 0.787 and 0.85 of the quote both got
  5.45 and 5.50; the same sheets gave 5.43 in one run and 5.57 in another. Falling-driver claims in
  round 1 (v10, 2 runs each): 5.40 and 5.30, and four counters instead of three. Hedge letter out
  of round 1: 5.52 (1 run). The forecast claim in place of the order prices next to the index:
  the same path 5.30, 5.20, 5.10 (1 run). A 5 % deadband clause sheet in round 1 got a first
  counter 1.5 to 2 % above the 0 % clause they add themselves (P08 5.60 to 5.64, P18 5.50; six
  runs on `steffen/elicit`).
- **Job shops in RFQs** dropped 12 to 15 % on their first counter (Dralveck 36.00 to 30.0 or
  30.5, Fuchsreiter 38.50 to 31.50, DEMO-J1 17.10 to 14.99). An anchor above a bidder's quote was
  agreed at once (P05 first run, 0.01). Dralveck agreed at our second sheet in every run: at a
  held anchor 27.86 (0.828) and 27.92 (0.822), at 28.03 to 28.07 after an 8 % step toward it
  (0.806 to 0.81). A 3 % deeper anchor (26.79) got a lower first counter (30.0), one more
  concession to 28.0 after the hold ("you only moved a few cents, but I want to keep our machines
  running"), then a walk-away at a cumulative gap of 39 % (`practice-v12-P05.log`, 0.746 on
  Fuchsreiter).
- **Later rounds.** D01: concessions of about min(0.8 x our move, 1.6 %, 0.8 %, 0.6 %, 0.4 %,
  0.2 % by round), final in round 6 at the latest or after a move of ours under 0.1 %; a constant
  sheet got no concession and a final in round 4. Donautal and Werdenfels: counters of +0.04 to
  +0.20; final in round 2 after a +1 % move, round 3 after a 30 % move, round 4 after three 30 %
  moves; a 55 % move got a hold and a higher price (5.55 to 5.58); 40 % got the same 0.10 as 30 %
  (2 runs); a slow walk of 12 % of the gap per round got five counters and 5.31 against four and
  5.33 to 5.39 (`50502ff781d898c6`). Leitner: 3.5 %, 2.2 %, 1.1 %, final in round 3 (5 of 5).
  Nordmark: 0.93, 0.88, 0.30, 0.07 EUR, "as you cannot commit to a binding higher volume, our
  flexibility is exhausted". Kalwisz: three steps of 0.50, then 45.50 at 300 ppm and at 800 ppm
  (`1f36a83c6e80e818`, `a74b89173c96c23c`); 300 ppm priced +0.50 over 1500. Ravensteiner: 2
  counters.
- **Counters per supplier over 115 practice threads:** Nordmark 1 to 6, Donautal 2 to 6,
  Werdenfels 2 to 6, Kalwisz 4 to 6. Its move as a share of our previous move (median, rounds 3
  on): Brandlhuber 0.62, Donautal 0.44, Werdenfels 0.45, Leitner 0.36, Nordmark 0.15, Kalwisz
  0.0, Selvbrunn and Wälzlager 0.0.
- **Cumulative gap at the final** (sum over rounds of our distance to its counter, relative):
  36 to 42 % (D01, P07, P08, P18); Nordmark walked at 19 % with sheets 2 to 7 % below its counter
  (P02 v1), Ravensteiner finalled in round 1 at 15 % (P10 v1). D01 walked after one sheet 0.1
  below its final ("absolute limit"). Nordmark, from an anchor of 345 with its clause: 351.05,
  349.85, 349.35, 349.05, then withdrew (`ea485d8c4db527aa`, 0).
- **`agreed` freezes the price:** after it, claims and pushes got "Our agreed offer stands"
  (16 of 19 early threads); P02 moved 0.7 % for 14-day payment once; a sheet above an agreed
  price closed at the higher price (P10).
- **Words, D01, identical sheets, 1 run each:** plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and acknowledging
  its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further?" 49.40. The same question
  every round on practice got "volume!" where volume was fixed, then no movement (P05, P18).
  Bluff and urgency on an unchanged sheet: same price, "built on mutual reliability, not on
  pressure" (3 runs each). Content-free "we need a better price" e-mails still got 52.90, 51.90,
  51.40, 51.10, 50.90. A fully model-written e-mail (figures and IDs guarded, `steffen/elicit`
  `086acb8`, 2 runs each): P02 0.733 and P18 0.630 to the cent as the template, P11 45.50, P08
  0.60 and 0.57 against 0.56 (spread of identical runs 0.47 to 0.67).
- **Asks** (829 supplier e-mails): "Which volume can you commit to?" 152, "A binding higher
  volume would help us" 62, faster payment 69 (Kalwisz five times, then "you just ignore it" and a
  final), proof of the forecast 30. Answering them in words registered ("allows us to review our
  pricing", "we have factored your confirmed volume") with prices inside the usual spread (v8,
  P02, P11). Kalwisz read our payment history: "we often see late payments".
- **Reply delay and shop size** (125 sessions): 4 to 5 days and no validity: founder-run job
  shops, conceded up to 22 %; 2 to 3 days: family firms, 1.6 to 13 %; 1 to 2 days: groups, 0 to
  12 %.
- **Several sheets:** the supplier picks one and answers it (D02, P03, P08). Offered a fixed sheet
  and a clause sheet in one message, Nordmark picked the clause (`91d2b5ad7501ce55`).
- **Timeouts** count as a round and "no move"; DEMO-J1 once answered one with a lower price; a
  deliberate one on D01 gave nothing (1 run). A crash after a final offer let the clock run out
  and Ravensteiner withdrew; a session does not pause while our process is down. Supplier
  replies take 19 s median, 28 s p90 (121 moves); our writer 1.8 s median, 6.3 s max; with N
  bidders a thread waits about (N - 1) x 21 s between our messages (3 bidders: 44 s, 66 s at p90;
  P05 had one late move).
- **Payment days at the supplier's own rate:** distributors 0 (free), Selvbrunn about 4 %/yr,
  Nordmark 6 % (about 0 by its cost breakdown), Wälzlager 7 %, Leitner 8.5 %, Hrvelec 12 to 17 %
  (45 to 90 days +1.5 to 2.1 %).
- **Contract length and clauses:** P03, P04, P07, P10 took 24 months at their price; in P10 it
  unlocked the full volume. Distributors refused 24 months fixed ("cannot maintain a fixed price
  for a 24-month term") and every deadband, offering an AS-14404 clause instead. Keeping our fixed
  sheet while they countered with their clause: P18 closed at 5.00 with the clause (0.688,

    def trade_sheets(self, s, main):
        """The lead's trades as extra sheets next to our opening sheet `main`: each changes one
        term and carries the price at which it costs us exactly what `main` costs, so whichever
        the supplier picks, we lose nothing and learn what it values. A trade whose price would
        sit at or above what the supplier quotes for those terms, or far below it, is not offered."""
        case, out = self.case, []

        for trade in s.trades:
            terms = {**main, trade["field"]: trade["value"]}
            if terms == main or not eco.must_haves_ok(case, terms, s.std):
                continue
            lo, hi = 0.0, main["unit_price"] * 3
            if (
                not eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, lo), s.std, s.est)
                < c_main

            ):

            for _ in range(50):  # C rises with the price
                mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                lo, hi = (mid, hi) if eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, mid), s.std, s.est) < c_main else (lo, mid)
            sheet = eco.at_price(terms, int(lo * 100) / 100)
            quoted = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, eco.value(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.quote), s.est))
            if not TRADE_MIN * quoted <= sheet["unit_price"] < 0.995 * quoted:
                continue
            out.append(sheet)
            self.note(s.sid, "trade_sheet", trade=trade, price=sheet["unit_price"], quoted=round(quoted, 2))
        return out

def step(last, theirs, conceded, first, fraction, budget, used, term_change=False):
    """Our next price after `last` against its counter `theirs`: we close `fraction` of the gap,
    hold low after a large first concession, and stay within the patience budget (`used` of it is
    spent). The real bidding and the demo bidding (`rehearsal.py`) both step with this."""
    gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
    share = fraction
    if first and conceded >= DEEP and not term_change:
        # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
        # P05, D02) and agrees at our sheet next: hold the anchor (Dralveck agreed at a held
        # 27.86, at 28.07 after an 8 % step); a drop that came with terms it added (an index
        # clause, P08, P18) is not one
        share = 0.0
    left = max(0.0, budget - used)
    new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
    if budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
        new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
    price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
    price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
    price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
    return max(price, last)

content.text:
The writeup is accurate where I could check it: every constant and mechanism I traced matches the code, and the results figures match `docs/learnings.md`. What needs fixing before 12:00 is the results framing, a few imprecise observations and getting the file onto `main`; it is 10:41 now.

I checked against `buyer/policy.py`, `research.py`, `rehearsal.py`, `analyst.py`, `memory.py` and `docs/learnings.md`. I did not recompile the `.tex` or re-derive scores from the session logs.

## Fix before submitting

1. **`writeup/` is untracked.** The README and `docs/design.md` now point to `writeup/writeup.pdf`, but neither file is committed. It has to go through a PR to `main` before the 12:00 hash, or the jury's repo has dead links.
2. **Results omit the two less flattering figures.** `docs/learnings.md` records a dashboard reference of 0.802 at the time of the 0.777 batch, and a 0.727 mean for the last ten-case validation run of one code version. The writeup gives only 0.777 (one batch) and 0.776 (best-of per case). Add at least the 0.727, since the two near-identical numbers read as a replication, which they are not.
3. **"Final offers arrived at a cumulative gap of 15 to 19 %" is not quite what happened.** Per the learnings, Nordmark withdrew at 19 % and only Ravensteiner gave a final offer, at 15 % in round 1. Write "final offers or withdrawals".
4. **"All twelve suppliers asked declined a cost breakdown" needs "practice".** The same learnings entry notes the D02 sandbox shop did send one, and §5 opens by saying the observations cover sandbox and practice.

## Worth one sentence each

- **The wave cap is never introduced.** §4 refers to "the time limit of a wave", but §1 mentions only the round limit and the 60 s deadline. Add the five waves of 8 minutes to §1.
- **Unseen suppliers.** The final has new suppliers and case types, and the writeup's only word on that is "where no data exist". Say that the Sunday release and the case's own facts are read at runtime; that also answers the brief's "what it reads in the data".
- **The 51.30 / 50.00 example has no scale.** Add the quotation of 52.90 and that it comes from 30 sandbox runs.
- **Writer reliability is left out.** The same batch logged 37 writer attempts with 29 successes; the rest fell back to the template. You report the subagent figure (121 of 127) but not this one, which is the weaker of the two.
- **"Holds its position"** after a deep first concession: the code still moves the minimum 0.2 % per sheet. "Moves only the minimum step" is exact.

## Outside the writeup

- `docs/design.md` says full cost is the should-cost "moved by its drivers' index change"; `policy.full_cost` returns the should-cost unchanged. The writeup matches the code; `design.md` is the stale one.
- `docs/README.md:8` still names `how-it-works.pdf`, which no longer exists.

The figure, layout and two-page length are fine, and the limitations paragraph is honest. I can apply the edits to the `.tex` and the two doc lines, but rebuilding the PDF needs `tectonic` on your machine.
